Both are presidential letters concerning the same Highway Safety Conference and its Action Program; both recount declining fatality rates while stressing that rising traffic volume leaves an urgent problem; and both seek stronger implementation through State and local action. The child materially reuses and adapts that framework to national-defense transportation needs. C05 contains closely related Action Program language and C19 supplies a parallel defense-driven reexamination and resource-conservation mechanism, but C14 is the closest overall template.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The Action Program developed by the President's Highway Safety Conference has proved most successful in the reduction of traffic accidents.","parent_excerpt":"I am calling a national meeting of the Highway Safety Conference... to stimulate application of the Action Program in the States","explanation":"Both letters organize the requested action around further State-level implementation of the same named Conference program."},{"child_excerpt":"The remarkable reduction of the traffic fatality rate from 11.3 per 100 million vehicle miles of travel in 1945 to less than 7 during the first 6 months of 1950... Despite the reduction in rate... In view of vastly increased traffic volume, the need for further application of the Action Program is evident.","parent_excerpt":"The rate of approximately 12 deaths per hundred-million vehicle-miles... dropped to 7.7 in 1948... Yet... as a result of the mounting travel on our roads and streets, the traffic death toll still exceeds 30,000 human lives a year.","explanation":"The child repeats C14's distinctive argumentative sequence: quantify the falling fatality rate, contrast it with continued deaths amid increasing travel, and use that contrast to justify renewed action."},{"child_excerpt":"request the States, communities and private groups concerned with the problem to increase emphasis on highway safety activities","parent_excerpt":"stimulate application of the Action Program in the States, particularly through the adaptation of the Program to the needs of communities and rural areas","explanation":"The operative appeal to intensify the program through States and communities substantially parallels C14's administrative approach."}]}
